title: Workflow Quality and Maintainability knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which statement correctly describes Workflow Quality and Maintainability?
options: Run untrusted pull-request code in the same job that holds production credentials.
Maintainable workflow design uses clear names, small jobs, tested shared logic, reviewed permission changes, and documentation that explains ownership and recovery.
Give every job write permission to avoid troubleshooting authorization errors.
Print all environment variables and event payloads to make the run easier to debug.
questions.answer_key: Maintainable workflow design uses clear names, small jobs, tested shared logic, reviewed permission changes, and documentation that explains ownership and recovery.
questions.explanation: This is the central behavior of workflow quality and maintainability: Maintainable workflow design uses clear names, small jobs, tested shared logic, reviewed permission changes, and documentation that explains ownership and recovery. Validate configuration and behavior against the current official reference before production use.

questions.prompt: How should a reviewer verify a change related to workflow quality and maintainability?
options: Publish the workflow to production before reviewing its triggers and permissions.
Run a controlled test or static check, inspect the relevant job and step result, and compare the evidence with the stated acceptance criteria.
Assume the workflow is correct as soon as the YAML file is committed.
Retry every failure without looking at the exit code or preserving evidence.
questions.answer_key: Run a controlled test or static check, inspect the relevant job and step result, and compare the evidence with the stated acceptance criteria.
questions.explanation: Reliable verification uses observable evidence. For this lesson, consider: Maintainable workflow design uses clear names, small jobs, tested shared logic, reviewed permission changes, and documentation that explains ownership and recovery. A syntax check alone cannot prove remote execution, permissions, or deployment behavior.
